newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq's Aziz slams U.S. secretary of state.
newsitem.headline: Iraq's Aziz slams U.S. secretary of state.

text.p: Iraqi Deputy Prime Minister Tareq Aziz on Thursday lambasted U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright, saying her comments on Iraq were an expression of "failing aspirations".
"Such American stands (toward Iraq) which were expressed by Albright...are an expression of failing aspirations," said Aziz in a statement carried by the official Iraqi News Agency.
"All American attempts aiming at...Iraq's national leadership have failed," he added.

The agency said Aziz's statement was in response to Albright's remarks in which she said the U.S. intended to back a political opposition in Iraq and laid out an explicit U.S. commitment to improve ties with a new government in Baghdad.

"Clearly, a change in Iraq's government could lead to a change in U.S. policy. Should that occur, we would stand ready, in coordination with our allies and friends, to enter rapidly into a dialogue with the successor regime," said Albright on Wednesday in a speech to Georgetown University.

The State Department denied she was urging an overthrow of Iraqi leader Saddam Hussein, who has been the target of relentless U.S. opposition since Washington in 1991 led an international coalition to repel Iraq's invasion of Kuwait.

The Iraqi deputy premier said Albright's remarks revealed the "United States has been using the (U.N.) security council and its affiliated establishments as a cover to achieve its own goals in the (Gulf) region in order to control its wealth".
The U.S. strongly backs the continuation of tough U.N. sanctions on Iraq which will not be lifted before Baghdad's full compliance with U.N. Security Council resolutions.
Aziz said his government had cooperated earnestly with the United Nations and the sanctions should have been lifted a long time ago but were prolonged by Washington.
